en: Abu Kurayb narrated it to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asking for hospitality, but he had nothing with which to host him. So he said: "Is there not a man who will host this person, may Allah have mercy on him?" A man from the Ansar called Abu Talhah stood up and took him to his dwelling... and he related the hadith in the manner of the hadith of Jarir, and mentioned therein the revelation of the verse as Waki' mentioned it.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man from the Ansar had a guest stay the night with him, and he had nothing except his food and the food of his children. So he said to his wife: "Put the children to sleep, extinguish the lamp, and serve the guest what you have." He said: Thereupon this verse was revealed: "...and give [them] preference over themselves, even though they are in privation." [Al-Hashr 59:9].

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Hazim al-Ashja'i, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "I am stricken by hunger and distress." So he sent a message to one of his wives, but she said: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, I have nothing except water." Then he sent to another, and she said the same thing, until all of them said the same thing: "No, by the One Who sent you with the truth, I have nothing except water." Thereupon he said: "Who will host this man tonight, may Allah have mercy on him?" A man from the Ansar stood up and said: "I will, O Messenger of Allah." So he took him to his dwelling and said to his wife: "Do you have anything?" She said: "No, except the food for my children." He said: "Distract them with something, and when our guest enters, extinguish the lamp and make him think that we are eating, and when he reaches out to eat, stand up to the lamp and put it out." He said: So they sat and the guest ate. When morning came, he went to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Allah was pleased with—or marveled at—the deed of the two of you with your guest tonight."

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir and Ahmad ibn Sa'id ibn Sakhr narrated to me—and their wordings are close—they said: Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us—in the narration of Hajjaj: Ibn Yazid Abu Zayd al-Ahwal—'Asim narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Aflah the freed slave of Abu Ayyub, from Abu Ayyub, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stayed as a guest with him, so the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stayed on the ground floor and Abu Ayyub stayed on the upper floor. He said: Abu Ayyub woke up one night and said: "We are walking above the head of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)!" So they moved aside and spent the night in a corner, then he spoke to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), but the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The lower floor is more convenient." He said: "I will not be above a roof beneath which you are." So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) moved to the upper floor and Abu Ayyub to the ground floor. He used to prepare food for the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and when it was brought back to him, he would ask where his fingers had touched and follow the traces of his fingers. Once he prepared food for him containing garlic, and when it was returned to him, he asked where the fingers of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had touched, and it was said to him: "He did not eat." He was alarmed and went up to him and said: "Is it forbidden?" The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "No, but I dislike it." He said: "Then I dislike what you dislike"—or "what you disliked." He said: And the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to receive revelation.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah, with this chain of narration.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Jabir ibn Samurah, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: Whenever food was brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he would eat from it and send whatever remained of it to me. One day he sent me leftover food from which he had not eaten because there was garlic in it. I asked him: "Is it forbidden?" He said: "No, but I dislike it because of its smell." He said: "Then I dislike what you disliked."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Abi Zaynab informed us, Abu Sufyan Talhah ibn Nafi' narrated to me, saying: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say: I was sitting in my house when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed by me and gestured to me, so I stood up and went to him. He took me by the hand, and we went until he came to one of the apartments of his wives. He entered, then gave me permission, so I entered behind the curtain upon her. He said: "Is there any lunch?" They said: "Yes." Three round loaves of bread were brought and placed on a platter. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) took one loaf and placed it before himself, took another loaf and placed it before me, then took the third and broke it in two, placing half of it before himself and half before me. Then he said: "Is there any condiment?" They said: "No, except a little vinegar." He said: "Bring it, for what an excellent condiment it is!"

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdhami narrated to us, my father narrated to me, al-Muthanna ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Nafi', Jabir ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) took him by the hand to his house... with the like of the hadith of Ibn 'Ulayyah up to his words: "for what an excellent condiment vinegar is," and he did not mention what came after it.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to me, Isma'il—meaning Ibn 'Ulayyah—narrated to us, from al-Muthanna ibn Sa'id, Talhah ibn Nafi' narrated to me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) took me by the hand one day to his home. Some pieces of bread were brought out for him, so he said: "Is there no condiment?" They said: "No, except a little vinegar." He said: "Indeed, vinegar is an excellent condiment." Jabir said: "I have continued to love vinegar ever since I heard it from the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." And Talhah said: "I have continued to love vinegar ever since I heard it from Jabir."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asked his family for a condiment, and they said: "We have nothing except vinegar." So he called for it and began eating with it, saying: "What an excellent condiment vinegar is! What an excellent condiment vinegar is!"

Musa ibn Quraysh ibn Nafi' al-Tamimi narrated it to us, Yahya ibn Salih al-Wuhazi narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, with this chain of narration, and he said: "What an excellent condiment," without doubt.

'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me, Yahya ibn Hassan informed us, Sulayman ibn Bilal informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "What an excellent condiment is vinegar."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: We were with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) at Marr al-Zahran while picking kabath (the ripe fruit of the arak tree). The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "You should choose the black ones among them." He said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, as if you have tended sheep?" He said: "Yes, and is there any prophet who did not tend them?"—or words to that effect.

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shabib narrated to us, he said: I heard it from Shahr ibn Hawshab, so I asked him and he said: I heard it from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr. He said: Then I met 'Abd al-Malik and he narrated to me from 'Amr ibn Hurayth, from Sa'id ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Truffles are a part of manna, and their water is a cure for the eye."

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, who said: I heard 'Amr ibn Hurayth saying: I heard Sa'id ibn Zayd saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Truffles are a part of the manna that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down upon the Children of Israel, and their water is a cure for the eye."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir informed us, from Mutarrif, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, from al-Hasan al-'Urani, from 'Amr ibn Hurayth, from Sa'id ibn Zayd, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Truffles are a part of the manna that Allah sent down upon Moses, and their water is a cure for the eye."

Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Ash'athi narrated to us, Abthar informed us, from Mutarrif, from al-Hakam, from al-Hasan, from 'Amr ibn Hurayth, from Sa'id ibn Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Truffles are a part of the manna that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down upon the Children of Israel, and their water is a cure for the eye."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me, Shu'bah narrated to us, he said: And al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah informed me, from al-Hasan al-'Urani, from 'Amr ibn Hurayth, from Sa'id ibn Zayd, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). Shu'bah said: "When al-Hakam narrated it to me, I did not find it unfamiliar after hearing the hadith of 'Abd al-Malik."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, who said: I heard 'Amr ibn Hurayth say: I heard Sa'id ibn Zayd say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Truffles are a part of manna, and their water is a cure for the eye."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir and 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd informed us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from 'Amr ibn Hurayth, from Sa'id ibn Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, who said: I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Truffles are a part of manna, and their water is a cure for the eye."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us—Yahya ibn Yahya said: "informed us," and the other two said: "narrated to us"—Isma'il—who is Ibn Ja'far—from Sharik—who is Ibn Abi Namir—from 'Abdullah ibn Abi 'Atiq, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, in the 'ajwah dates of al-'Aliyah there is healing, or they are an antidote in the early morning."

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated it to us, Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us, Abu Badr Shuja' ibn al-Walid informed us; both from Hashim ibn Hashim, with this chain of narration, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, and neither of them said: "I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hashim ibn Hashim, who said: I heard 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas say: I heard Sa'd say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Whoever takes seven 'ajwah dates in the morning, neither poison nor sorcery will harm him on that day."

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us, Sulayman—meaning Ibn Bilal—narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever eats seven dates from between its two lava tracts (the two volcanic plains of Medina) in the morning, no poison will harm him until evening."

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Muhammad ibn Tahla' narrated to us, from Abu al-Rijal Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his mother, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O 'A'ishah, a house in which there are no dates, its inhabitants are hungry. O 'A'ishah, a house in which there are no dates, its inhabitants are hungry"—or "its inhabitants go hungry." He said it twice or thrice.

'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me, Yahya ibn Hassan informed us, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The people of a house having dates will not go hungry."

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, they said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade that a man should eat two dates together at once (qiran) until he asks permission of his companions.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated it to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, both from Shu'bah, with this chain of narration; and there is not in the hadith of either of them the remark of Shu'bah, nor his statement: "and people had been stricken by hardship in those days."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, he said: I heard Jabalah ibn Suhaym say: Ibn al-Zubayr used to provide us with dates—he said—and people at that time had been stricken by hardship. We would be eating and Ibn 'Umar would pass by us while we were eating and say: "Do not eat two dates at a time, for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade eating two dates together (iqran), unless a man asks permission from his brother." Shu'bah said: "I think this phrase is only from the words of Ibn 'Umar"—meaning asking permission.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, both from Sufyan—Ibn Abi 'Umar said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Mus'ab ibn Sulaym, from Anas, who said: Dates were brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) began distributing them while sitting alertly on his haunches (muhtafizan), eating from them quickly. And in the narration of Zuhayr: "eating briskly."
